chunks: Even thus no apostle came to those before them but they said: 'He is a sorcerer or a mad man.'

key_terms.الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِم: those who were before them (previous nations)

ai.seo_question: What did people say about the prophets before them?
ai.summary: This verse from Surah Al-Dhariyat (51:52) underscores the historical continuity of rejection faced by prophets, a theme central to Shia exegesis which often links this skepticism to the specific accusations leveled against the Ahl al-Bayt and the Imams. By categorizing detractors as viewing messengers as 'magicians' or 'insane,' the text provides a theological framework for understanding the persistence of doubt despite clear signs, reinforcing the necessity of divine proof (hujjah).
